cohort: The study included 152,827 children born to women in the reproductive age group (15-49) who had their most recent live birth in the five years preceding the survey.
finding: Fetal macrosomia prevalence was 3.8%, with male neonates and those born to mothers who were overweight, obese, had gestational diabetes, hypertension, were multiparous, had inadequate ANC, or were Muslim or tribal women, having a significantly higher risk.
cross-section timing: Data were drawn from the fifth round of the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) regarding births in the five years preceding the survey.
